text: Making HTTP requests is the foundation of working with APIs. When your program sends a request, the server responds, often with data in JSON format, which is easy for computers to read. However, you usually need authentication, like an API key, to prove you have permission. Also, be aware of rate limits—servers might block you if you send too many requests too quickly. Most importantly, always include error handling in your code. Network problems or bad data can happen, so check the response status and handle failures gracefully. This way, your application stays reliable even when things go wrong.
